quizzes.stem: A developer wants Claude to study a repository and show a written draft before any file on disk changes. Which start fits?

options.a: The `default` mode, which asks about each action one by one
options.b: The `acceptEdits` mode, which writes edits without asking
options.d: The `dontAsk` mode, which denies whatever would prompt

explanation.c: The page says "Claude reads files and proposes a plan but makes no edits until you approve", and `claude --permission-mode plan` starts there.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the table lists `default` (Manual) for "Reviewing every action yourself", so it prompts action by action and no draft comes first.
explanation.b: Ruled out because `acceptEdits` runs "Reads, file edits, and common filesystem commands" without asking, so edits land on disk at once.
explanation.d: Ruled out because `dontAsk` runs "Reads and pre-approved tools; anything that would prompt is denied", so it denies and shows no draft.

quizzes.stem: A repository's shared settings file sets the starting permission mode to `bypassPermissions`. What happens when a teammate opens it?

options.a: The session starts in auto mode for every teammate who opens it
options.b: The value is ignored, and each edit and command asks first
options.c: The session starts in plan mode until the file is approved
options.d: Every teammate is asked once to accept the project file's mode

explanation.b: The page says a `"bypassPermissions"` set in those two files "doesn't take effect either, and the session starts in Manual mode".
explanation.a: Ruled out because that is exactly what the rule prevents, since "the value doesn't take effect".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the page names Manual mode and not plan mode: "the session starts in Manual mode".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "The other values apply from any settings file", and these two are the exceptions, so no prompt is shown.

quizzes.stem: Rules given early in a long conversation stop being followed. Where should a rule that must always apply be kept?

options.a: In a `/compact` summary, which condenses the thread so far
options.b: In a `/clear` command, which starts fresh on a new task
options.c: In a rewind checkpoint, which snapshots files before each edit
options.d: In `CLAUDE.md`, which sits outside the running chat

explanation.d: The page says "Put persistent rules in CLAUDE.md", because "Claude compacts automatically, but instructions from early in the conversation can get lost."
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Claude compacts automatically, but instructions from early in the conversation can get lost", so a summary is where they are lost.
explanation.b: Ruled out because `/clear` is described as one that "starts fresh on a new task while keeping project memory", so the rules must already be in the memory file.
explanation.c: Ruled out because checkpoints "only cover file changes", so a checkpoint holds files and not rules.

quizzes.stem: A repository holds credentials in `.env`, and Claude must never open them. One teammate writes a sentence about it in the memory file, and another adds a path block to the shared configuration. Which one actually stops it?

options.a: The `Read` rule, which is checked before each call runs
options.b: The memory sentence, which Claude Code enforces once it loads
options.c: Both entries equally, since each is read before any tool call
options.d: Neither entry, since a project file never beats a user file

explanation.a: The page says "Claude treats them as context, not enforced configuration", while "Rules are evaluated in order: deny, then ask, then allow."
explanation.b: Ruled out because memory files are "context, not enforced configuration", so the sentence only asks.
explanation.c: Ruled out because a memory file is loaded "at the start of every conversation" and still only asks, while a deny rule sits first in "deny, then ask, then allow".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "A key set at a higher level overrides the same key set lower down" is about the same key, and since "they combine across layers", a project deny still applies.

quizzes.stem: A settings file allows `Bash(git log *)` and another layer lists `Bash(git *)` under deny. What happens when Claude runs `git log --oneline`?

options.a: It is allowed, because the allow rule names the narrower command here
options.b: It is allowed, because the later layer replaces the earlier one in full
options.c: It asks, because the two rules cancel each other out in the end
options.d: It is refused, because rules of that kind are checked first and win

explanation.d: The page says "Rules are evaluated in order: deny, then ask, then allow. The first match in that order determines the outcome, and rule specificity doesn't change the order."
explanation.a: Ruled out because "rule specificity doesn't change the order", so a narrower allow does not win.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the first match decides and the rules never cancel: "An allow rule can't carve an exception out of a deny rule".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "they combine across layers", so the later layer does not replace the earlier one.

quizzes.stem: A developer wants to use a cheaper model on their own machine without changing it for the team. Where does the setting go?

options.a: The shared project file, which is committed with the code of the team
options.b: The managed settings, which override every other layer of the settings
options.c: The local project file, which is kept out of version control
options.d: The memory file, which names the model in one plain sentence of text

explanation.c: The page puts "A personal override" in the local file, which "belongs in `.gitignore`".
explanation.a: Ruled out because "The team's choices go in the shared project file, which is committed", so the choice would reach the whole team.
explanation.b: Ruled out because managed settings are for "A rule that must hold regardless of what any developer writes", and are not a personal file.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the memory file "asks" and does not set a model: "A memory file asks and a hook enforces."

quizzes.stem: A CI job runs `claude -p` to review each diff and must give the same result on every runner. Which flag is the key part?

options.a: `--output-format json`, because it gives a script structured text to parse
options.b: `--bare`, because it skips the local setup that discovery finds
options.c: `--max-turns`, because it limits how many agentic turns a single run takes
options.d: `--max-budget-usd`, because it caps the amount that a single run may spend

explanation.b: The page says `--bare` is "useful for CI and scripts where you need the same result on every machine."
explanation.a: Ruled out because "Use `json` when a script parses the result", which shapes the output and does not remove local configuration.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "`--max-turns` limits the number of agentic turns", which bounds a run and does not make two runners agree.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "`--max-budget-usd` caps the spend", which is a bound on cost and not on configuration.

quizzes.stem: A command's workflow deploys code and posts to an external service. How is Claude kept from launching it on its own judgement?

options.a: Add an `argument-hint` line to its frontmatter
options.b: Save it as a command file and not as a skill folder

explanation.c: The page says setting `disable-model-invocation: true` tells it to "prevent Claude from automatically loading this skill", so only a person can start it.
explanation.a: Ruled out because `argument-hint` is "a hint such as `[issue-number]` shown in autocomplete" and controls nobody.
explanation.b: Ruled out because a command file and a skill "both create `/deploy` and work the same way", so the file kind changes nothing.
explanation.d: Ruled out because `dontAsk` "runs reads and pre-approved tools and denies anything that would prompt", which decides tool approval and not who may load a command.

quizzes.stem: A script lists `--allowedTools "Bash"` so that a headless review can run `git diff`. What is wrong with it?

options.a: It pre-approves every shell command, because a bare name matches all
options.b: It is rejected at start, because a tool name must carry a pattern
options.c: It is skipped by a bare run, because `--bare` ignores a tool list
options.d: It approves nothing, because only `dontAsk` can pre-approve a tool

explanation.a: The trap says "`--allowedTools "Bash"` approves every command. List `Bash(git diff *)` and its like."
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page says "List patterns and not whole tools that change things", a recommendation and not a parsing rule, and its own example lists a bare `Read`.
explanation.c: Ruled out because `--bare` skips "auto-discovery of hooks, skills, custom commands, subagents, installed plugins, MCP servers, auto memory, and CLAUDE.md", and a flag passed on the command line is not discovered.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the flag itself "pre-approves specific tools, in quotes and separated by commas", while `dontAsk` merely "runs reads and pre-approved tools".

quizzes.stem: A new repository has no memory file, and a developer needs a useful one by the end of the day. Which sequence fits?

options.a: Pull in a very large template with imports, then keep the main file short
options.b: Write every convention by hand, then run `/compact` on that file
options.c: Run `/init`, then add every convention the team has ever used
options.d: Run `/init`, then delete lines Claude would have found anyway

explanation.d: The page says `/init` "analyzes your codebase and creates a file with build commands, test instructions, and project conventions it discovers", then to "cut what Claude would have found anyway".
explanation.a: Ruled out because imports "don't reduce its context cost, because imported files also load at launch".
explanation.b: Ruled out because `/compact` is for the conversation: "use `/context` to see what fills the window and `/compact` to summarise it".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Longer files consume more context and reduce adherence", so adding everything works against the file.

quizzes.stem: A nightly script runs `claude -p` and sometimes loops on tool calls for an hour. Which pair of flags bounds it?

options.a: A turn limit and a spend cap on the run
options.b: A permission mode and a tool list for the run
options.c: A bare switch and a JSON output format on the run
options.d: A resume flag and a fork flag for the next run

explanation.a: The page says "`--max-turns` limits the number of agentic turns, and `--max-budget-usd` caps the spend."
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Use `json` when a script parses the result", and bare mode only skips discovery, so neither bounds a loop.
explanation.b: Ruled out because "`--permission-mode dontAsk` runs reads and pre-approved tools", which decides what may run and not how long.
explanation.d: Ruled out because `--resume` reopens a session "under the same session ID and appends new messages to the existing conversation", which continues a loop and does not bound it.

quizzes.stem: A team wants the review script to inspect code and change nothing, with no prompt ever shown. Which setup fits?

options.a: `bypassPermissions`, with the runner as the only boundary
options.b: `auto`, with the classifier left to judge every single call
options.c: `dontAsk`, with `Read` and read-only git patterns listed
options.d: `acceptEdits`, with edits approved for the whole checkout

explanation.c: The page says `--permission-mode dontAsk` "runs reads and pre-approved tools and denies anything that would prompt, which fits a script", with `Read` and read-only git patterns.
explanation.b: Ruled out because auto mode "reviews actions instead of you" and runs most calls, not reads alone.
explanation.d: Ruled out because `acceptEdits` runs "Reads, file edits, and common filesystem commands", which is more than reads.
explanation.a: Ruled out because `bypassPermissions` is for "Isolated containers and VMs only", and it runs everything.

quizzes.stem: A developer in Manual mode is tired of approving each source change, but wants a prompt before every other action. Which mode fits?

options.a: `plan`, which makes no edits until a plan is approved
options.b: `acceptEdits`, which lets edits and filesystem commands run
options.c: `dontAsk`, which denies each action that would prompt
options.d: `auto`, where a second model reviews the actions instead

explanation.b: The table gives `acceptEdits` "Reads, file edits, and common filesystem commands", and other shell commands still ask.
explanation.a: Ruled out because plan mode is where "Claude reads files and proposes a plan but makes no edits until you approve", so changes wait for approval.
explanation.c: Ruled out because `dontAsk` "runs reads and pre-approved tools and denies anything that would prompt", so nothing asks.
explanation.d: Ruled out because auto mode runs "Everything, with background safety checks", so shell work does not prompt either.
